axis: an offer dangled → the trap sprung

members.tone: The lightest of the three: a promise held out to someone still standing free of it, where *lure* already has them moving.
Works by making the promise attractive rather than by baiting a spot, so the persuasion sounds pleasant even when it is the exaggerated kind.
Draws the person somewhere rather than merely dangling something, and of the three it keeps the falseness of the promise nearest the surface.
Neutral and technical here: the enticement is a mimicked animal cry, so the whole of the deception sits in the sound and none of it in any promise.
The enticing is only half of it — the closing of the trap is the other half, which is what makes this land harder than *entice*.
